### Round log
- G1R1: baseline 1.000x, geomean 40.0ms. E0001 (substring-match selectivity) retired because the implementer ran out of time, not because the idea was bad.
- G1R2: E0002, a minimal version of E0001, built OK. Estimates moved but the physical plan did NOT change, so there was no gain. RETIRED. The premise was wrong.

### Lessons for dispatching
- Keep diffs out of widely included headers (long rebuilds). Use file-local statics or constexpr.
- Ask implementers to build in the background and to EXPLAIN-check before the full bench.
- CHEAP EXPERIMENTS: `dbe-tool sql "SET <setting>=X; <query>; <query>"` prints per-statement ms (first run cold, second hot). Use it for investigation only.
- rules.md item 4: never change default settings.
- Planner estimates after LIKE filters and outer joins are off by 5-1000x. Prefer runtime-adaptive mechanisms.
- The bar is -2.7% visible geomean. A 20% gain on one of 14 templates (about -1.6% geomean) does NOT clear it on its own. Pick changes that cut a big template by 30%+ or help several templates.

### Tooling facts
- EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) hangs. EXPLAIN ANALYZE via `dbe-tool sql` works.
- Grep profile.md with `│ +[A-Z_]{5,} +│|[0-9]\.[0-9]+s +│|[0-9,]+ rows +│` to get operator timings.
- profile.md truncates big plans. Operator times are summed CPU.
- Bench noise is about ±10% per query on quick runs.

### Codebase facts (verified)
- HASH_JOIN: the LEFT child is the probe and the RIGHT child is the build.
- Join BF: CanUseBloomFilter physical_hash_join.cpp:761 requires conditions.size()==1. FinalizeFilters :814 loops over filter_idx and probe_info. BF pushes are deferred (sink.deferred_bloom_filters :212, pushed at :587 in FinishEvent). PushBloomFilter :787 uses conditions[0].
- The HT BF is filled in JoinHashTable::Finalize join_hashtable.cpp:775, from the stored combined row hash, via InsertHashes :717. It is allocated in AllocatePointerTable :741 when should_build_bloom_filter is set. BFTableFilter probes with VectorOperations::Hash of one column (bloom_filter.cpp:90). So a multi-key BF needs a per-key gather+hash on the build side.
- LIKE: LikeMatcher is already good. FSST scan decompresses every row.
- RelationStatisticsHelper::DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY=0.2 applies flat to non-equality filters.
- Perfect hash agg: CanUsePerfectHashAggregate plan_aggregate.cpp:127, threshold :230. PerfectAggregateHashTable has eager init (perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp:36-48). E0004 had a working lazy version.
  - Measured: q13 inner agg forced perfect 115→90ms. A 23-bit perfect table on 6M rows is 10x slower. A 20-bit table on empty input costs +10ms.
- Radix HT adaptation: DecideAdaptation radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424, MaybeRepartition :479.

### Profile hotspots (G3R1, geomean 41.3ms)
- q09 114ms, q13 98, q18 81, q19 50, q16 44, q22 43, rest 21-35ms.
- q09: hash join probes ~0.24s CPU each, lineitem scan 0.43s. partsupp (800k) gets only min/max filters.
- q13: orders scan + NOT LIKE 0.22s, RIGHT join 0.10-0.15s, HASH_GROUP_BY 0.20s.
- q18: subquery GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING over 6M rows (~76ms standalone), 1.5M groups.

### Directions
- Active: multi-key join BF (G3R1). If it fails because of an implementation bug, retry. If the BF is not selective in practice (check EXPLAIN rows on the partsupp scan), the direction is exhausted.
- Next candidates: q18 high-cardinality agg (backlog issue; profile first). q19 OR-filter, q16 and q22 not investigated yet; look at their plans in profile.md next round. Possibly combine the lazy perfect HT (E0004) with another agg win.
- Exhausted: cardinality-selectivity tweaks for q09; estimate-gated perfect hashing; standalone lazy perfect HT (correct, but too small a gain).

issues.title: Per-key bloom filter pushdown for multi-key hash joins
issues.hypothesis: In q09 (the slowest template, 114ms) the 2-key join partsupp ⋈ (filtered part/lineitem build side, ~324k rows) probes all 800k partsupp rows. Its probe costs ~0.14-0.16s CPU, and the scan only gets min/max dynamic filters, because JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:775) requires ht->conditions.size()==1. The only reason is that the HT bloom filter is filled with the combined hash of all keys (JoinHashTable::Finalize join_hashtable.cpp:790 loads the stored row hash, and InsertHashes :721 inserts it into bloom_filter). BFTableFilter::Filter (bloom_filter.cpp:90-92) probes with VectorOperations::Hash of the single filter column. A BF on one key column needs that column hashed on its own. ps_partkey alone is very selective here, since p_name LIKE '%ghost%' keeps ~5% of parts. A partkey BF would drop ~95% of partsupp rows in the scan before the probe and the hash computation. The SelectivityOptionalFilter wrapper (BF_THRESHOLD/BF_CHECK_N) already switches off a BF on an unselective key such as ps_suppkey, so pushing a filter on every equality key is safe.
issues.plan: 1) join_hashtable.hpp/.cpp: keep the existing single-key bloom_filter path as it is. Add per-key bloom filters for multi-key equality joins, e.g. `vector<unique_ptr<BloomFilter>> key_bloom_filters` indexed by condition index, plus setter/getter. In AllocatePointerTable (:741), Initialize each requested one with Count(). In Finalize (:775), for each requested key: Gather that key column from row_locations into a Vector (data_collection->Gather with an incremental sel, as at :968/:1487). First verify which layout column holds condition i; equality keys may be reordered (see equality_predicate_columns). Then VectorOperations::Hash it into a hash vector and call key_bf.InsertHashes(hash_vec, count). Only do this work when a key BF was requested. 2) physical_hash_join.cpp: in CanUseBloomFilter, allow conditions.size()>1 when cmp == COMPARE_EQUAL (keep the build_side_has_filter and probe-larger checks). In FinalizeFilters (:899), for multi-key joins, record the condition index join_condition[filter_idx] in the deferred entry and request the key BF for that condition. In PushBloomFilter (:787), for multi-key joins, use that condition's BF, NullValuesAreEqual(cond_idx), conditions[cond_idx].right->ToString() and left->return_type instead of index 0. The deferred vector's pair type may need a third field (a struct or tuple), so update the declarations at physical_hash_join.cpp:212 and join_filter_pushdown.hpp:86. 3) Before the full bench, check with EXPLAIN ANALYZE of q09 that the partsupp scan shows an 'IN BF' dynamic filter on ps_partkey, and that its row count falls from 800k to under 100k. Build in the background, since join_hashtable.hpp is included by the join operators.
issues.expected_gain: q09: 10-20% (partsupp probe ~0.15s CPU plus scan and hash work on 800k rows). Small gains are possible on other multi-key equality joins where the build side is filtered. Geomean maybe -1.5% to -3%.
issues.generality: Any equi-join on a composite key (partsupp/lineitem-style composite keys, multi-column fact-to-dimension joins, decorrelated subqueries correlated on 2+ columns) where the build side is filtered. Possible slowdowns: multi-key joins with large unselective build sides pay an extra gather, hash and BF insert per key on the build. The check that the probe is larger than the build, and SelectivityOptionalFilter on the probe side, limit this.
issues.risk: Medium. Correctness depends on mapping each condition index to its layout column and on matching hash semantics. The BF must hash exactly like VectorOperations::Hash on the probe column type; skip keys whose probe column has a cast (has_cast is already checked). NULL handling must use the per-condition NullValuesAreEqual. A header change means a longer rebuild.
